title: Ableton-style UI, music ducking while you talk, and a better AI brain
question: A (UX-16): which 5-6 interface elements make a DAW feel pro and fast, ranked for Studio Keys, with the smallest change for each. B (AI-10): how voice assistants, DJ talkover and DAWs duck music, and the browser defaults to use. C (AI-11): stronger text models on Workers AI and Claude, cost per 100 requests, and which 2 to test.
bottomLine: A: Studio Keys reads as a scrolling web page; the biggest Ableton win is a one-screen studio frame (thin control bar, dense track lanes, a bottom Clip/Device panel, the controller in a drawer), shipped in 6 small steps. B: duck the music about -15 dB in 60-80 ms when 'Keys' is heard, hold it through the command and the reply, release over about 0.8 s, never duck during a recorded take, and feed Web Speech an echo-cancelled mic track (Chrome 135+). C: test gpt-oss-120b on Workers AI (free tier, about $0.20 per 100 requests, the same as Llama today) against Claude Haiku 5.5 (already wired in; owner's key; about $0.02-0.06 per 100 requests); DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is the reserve if the owner has Workers Paid; avoid Kimi K2.6, Nemotron 3 and GLM-5.3-flash (planned deprecation 20 Nov 2026 has passed).
findings: Live 12 is one fixed window: Control Bar on top, Browser on the left, Session/Arrangement in the centre, Clip/Device detail at the bottom, Info View bottom-left; themes are neutral and matte, and colour lives on tracks and clips.
Bitwig toggles panels with single keys from footer icons and has an Inspector for the selected item; FL Studio's Hint Bar explains whatever is under the mouse.

Studio Keys at 1440x900: the first screen is the hardware controller, and the DAW starts about 820 px down. Tracks are rounded cards (300 px header, 6 px gaps, 12 px radius), the mixer is 360 px horizontal cards, and transport controls are split over two rows.
Typical duck depths: Android -14 dB (factor 0.2); Pioneer DJM talkover -18 dB by default (range -6 to -24, with a mids-only Advanced mode); Home Assistant voice satellite -6 dB.

Voice-over ducking practice: attack 10-30 ms, release 300-700 ms; releases of 250 ms or less make the music bounce back between words. Cars should not unduck between an assistant's back-to-back phrases.

Music behind speech sharply raises recognition errors at 0-5 dB speech-to-music ratio (a clean-trained model went from 11% to 47-79% word errors); echo cancellation gives large gains for the device's own playback.

Chrome 135+ lets SpeechRecognition.start(track) take a getUserMedia track. Chrome's echo canceller removes the page's own Web Audio output on the default device, not other apps' audio. Today the app starts recognition on the raw mic.

Workers AI: 10,000 free neurons/day, then $0.011 per 1,000 neurons; Kimi, GLM-5.x and DeepSeek V4 models need Workers Paid. Per 100 requests (4.5k in + 300 out): Llama 3.3 $0.20, gpt-oss-120b about $0.20, Llama 4 Scout $0.15, Gemma 4 $0.05, Qwen3.8 $0.43, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash $0.17 ($0.04 cached), Kimi K2.6 $0.55.

Anthropic: Haiku 5.5 costs $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens ($0.06 per 100 requests, about $0.02 with prompt caching); Sonnet 5.5 costs $2/$10 ($1.20 per 100, about $0.35 cached). The Worker already supports Claude through ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
recommendations: UX-16 (studio-ux-dev): ship in this order: 1) one-screen frame at 1024 px and wider, with the controller as a drawer; 2) flat dense track lanes with colour only on clips; 3) a single 40 px control bar; 4) a bottom Clip/Device panel (Shift+Tab); 5) 76 px vertical mixer strips; 6) a 240 px browser sidebar plus a one-line hint strip. Phones keep the current tab bar.

AI-10 (sound-engine-dev): add a master 'duck' GainNode before the limiter, moved only with setTargetAtTime; -15 dB while the user talks, -10 dB while Keys speaks, 60-80 ms attack, 500 ms hold, about 0.8 s release; optional mid-cut style; never during a recorded take or count-in.

AI-10 (assistant-dev): duck on the first interim result containing 'Keys' or on an orb press; open an echo-cancelled assistant mic and call rec.start(track) on Chrome 135+, falling back to rec.start(); keep the singing mic with AEC off.

AI-11 (assistant-dev, lead): put the model behind a variable and run a 20-prompt side-by-side of gpt-oss-120b (reasoning_effort low) against Claude Haiku 5.5 (with prompt caching). Score valid JSON, correct actions, single-element edits and reply time; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is the reserve if Workers Paid.
